passage: NOTICE TO MEMBERS: The pool will be closed from Monday to Wednesday next week while the water system is being checked. The fitness room and the tennis courts will stay open as usual. Members who have already paid for swimming lessons on those days may either move them to the following week or ask for their money back at the front desk.
q: What can a member with a swimming lesson next Tuesday do?

qGloss.zh: 下周二有游泳课的会员可以怎么办？

opts: Change the day or get a refund
Pay again at the front desk
Use the tennis courts for free

passage: Hi Nadia, I'm so sorry, but I won't be able to come to your housewarming on Saturday after all. My cousin's flight has been changed, and I've been asked to pick her up from the airport at exactly that time. If you're free on Sunday, could I come over then and bring the cake I promised? I'd still love to see your new place. Tomas
q: Why is Tomas writing to Nadia?

qGloss.zh: Tomas 为什么给 Nadia 写这条消息？

opts: To explain a change of plan and suggest a new one
To invite her to see his new home on Sunday
To ask her to collect his cousin from the airport
To say that he will arrive late on Saturday

passage: Mina had checked the clock at least twenty times. The bus from the capital was supposed to arrive at four, and it was already half past. She walked to the window again. Three years was a long time. Would her brother still laugh at her jokes? Would he even look the same? Then she heard an engine outside, and her heart jumped.
q: How does Mina feel as she waits?

qGloss.zh: Mina 等待的时候心情怎么样？

passage: Many people believe you need hours of free time to learn a new language. Elif, a bus driver, disagrees. For two years she has listened to ten minutes of Spanish during each break and repeated the sentences aloud. "Short and often works better than long and rare," she says. Last month she had her first full conversation with a tourist.
q: What does Elif's story suggest?

qGloss.zh: Elif 的故事说明了什么？

opts: Living abroad can speed up learning
Long lessons can make up for missed days
Regular short practice can bring real results

passage: After many requests, the reading room will now stay open until midnight on weekdays during the exam period. Please note that this is a trial. Staff will count how many people are present after ten o'clock each night, and the longer hours will continue next term only if the numbers justify the cost. In other words, if you asked for this, now is the time to use it.
q: What does the last sentence imply?

qGloss.zh: 最后一句话暗示了什么？

opts: The room will be too crowded to use
Late opening may end if few people come
Staff need volunteers to help them count
People who asked for it must pay extra

passage: Dear Ingrid Lindqvist, Thank you for sending us your book, which our team read with interest. Your descriptions of the northern coast are beautiful, and several of us did not want to put it down. Unfortunately, our list for the next two years is already full, and we would not be able to give your work the attention it deserves. We wish you every success in placing it elsewhere.
q: What is the main purpose of this email?

qGloss.zh: 这封邮件的主要目的是什么？

opts: To ask for changes to the book
To offer to publish it in two years
To turn the book down politely
To request more chapters to read

passage: When the letter finally came, Arjun left it on the kitchen table for two days. He made tea beside it, read the newspaper beside it, and once moved it to wipe the table underneath. His sister, visiting on the third morning, picked it up, looked at the university's name on the envelope, and then looked at him. "You know," she said, "waiting won't change what's inside."
q: Why has Arjun not opened the letter?

qGloss.zh: Arjun 为什么一直没有拆开这封信？

opts: He wants his sister to read it first
He already knows what it says
He has not noticed it on the table
He is afraid of what it may say

passage: Grandfather's workshop had one rule: nothing was thrown away. Bent nails were straightened; broken chairs waited years for the right piece of wood. As a child, I assumed he simply could not bear to spend a coin. It was only when I watched him turn a cracked table into a bookshelf for the family next door, refusing any payment, that I understood. He was not saving money. He was saving things.
q: What did the writer come to understand about the grandfather?

qGloss.zh: 作者后来明白了祖父的什么？

opts: He kept things out of care, not love of money
He was much poorer than he had seemed
He thought that repairing things wasted time

passage: Critics of the new library complain that it resembles a hotel lobby, and they are not wrong: there are sofas, a snack bar, even background music. What they overlook is that the old building, for all its dignified silence, was visited by fewer than two hundred people a week. A library that nobody enters preserves books admirably and readers not at all.
q: What is the writer's position?

qGloss.zh: 作者的立场是什么？

opts: The critics are wrong but mean well
The new library is an embarrassing mistake
The old building served readers better
The critics are right but miss the point

passage: A survey found that people who eat breakfast earn more than those who skip it, a result promptly reported as proof that the morning meal leads to success. It would be just as reasonable, on this evidence, to conclude that being well paid gives one the leisure to eat in the morning. The data show that two things travel together; they are silent on which, if either, is doing the driving.
q: What point is the writer making?

qGloss.zh: 作者想说明什么？

opts: The survey's figures were probably invented
The survey cannot show what causes what
Well-paid people rarely have time to eat
Breakfast clearly leads to higher pay

passage: It has become fashionable to describe every minor inconvenience as a "crisis" and every competent employee as a "rock star". One wonders what vocabulary will be left when something truly serious or truly brilliant comes along. Inflation, as economists remind us, does not make anyone richer; it merely obliges us to hand over more coins for the same loaf. The same, I suspect, holds for words.
q: What is the writer's main concern?

qGloss.zh: 作者最担心的是什么？

opts: Employees receive far too much empty praise
Strong words lose their force through overuse
Ordinary goods cost more with every year

passage: Residents are reminded that the courtyard is a shared space. While the management has no wish to regulate how people enjoy it, the appearance over the summer of a trampoline, two sheds and what we understand to be a pizza oven suggests that some guidance may be overdue. A meeting will be held on the 14th.
q: What is the real message of this notice?

qGloss.zh: 这则通知真正想说的是什么？

opts: Some residents have overused the shared space
The management plans to close the courtyard
New equipment has been bought for everyone
Residents are invited to a summer party

passage: The new translation app promises "conversations without borders", and for ordering a meal or asking the way it does the job well enough. Ask it to handle a joke, a polite refusal or anything said between the lines, however, and it produces sentences that are grammatically perfect and socially awkward. As a phrasebook, it is impressive. As an interpreter, it has a long way to go.
q: What is the writer's attitude to the app?

qGloss.zh: 作者对这个应用的态度是什么？

opts: It is clever with jokes but weak on grammar
It is useless even for basic phrases
It is useful for simple tasks but oversold
It is impressive in every kind of conversation

passage: Every January, fitness clubs fill with new members, and by March most of them have vanished. The usual explanation is weak willpower. A more convincing one is poor planning: people choose goals that depend on feeling motivated, and motivation is the first thing to disappear on a cold, dark morning. Those who last tend to do something duller. They fix a time, lay out their shoes the night before, and stop asking themselves whether they feel like going.
q: According to the writer, why do some people keep exercising?

qGloss.zh: 按照作者的说法，为什么有些人能坚持锻炼？

opts: They have stronger willpower than others
They start in March instead of January
They rely on routine rather than on mood

passage: Our street's tool library was supposed to save everyone money: why own a drill you use twice a year? What nobody anticipated was the conversation. Borrowing a ladder means knocking on a door, and returning it tends to involve a cup of tea. Two years in, the drills are barely mentioned. Ask the residents what the project has given them, and they talk about knowing, at last, who lives at number nine.
q: According to the writer, what has been the main benefit of the tool library?

qGloss.zh: 按照作者的说法，这个工具图书馆带来的最大好处是什么？

opts: Fewer households now need to own a ladder
People on the street have come to know each other
Residents have saved a great deal of money
Residents have learned to repair things themselves

passage: For years the village of Tarn kept its famous spring a secret, fearing that visitors would spoil it. When a magazine finally published the location, the crowds came, and so did something nobody had predicted: money to repair the path, volunteers to clear up after picnics, and a team of locals who now guard the place more closely than ever. The spring, people admit a little awkwardly, has never looked better.
q: What does the text suggest about the publicity?

qGloss.zh: 关于这次曝光，文中暗示了什么？

opts: It ended up protecting what the villagers feared losing
It caused the damage the villagers had expected
It made very little difference to the spring
It was secretly arranged by the villagers themselves

passage: The consultant's report ran to two hundred pages, the first hundred and ninety of which established, with admirable thoroughness, that the company had a problem. The remedy occupied the final ten and consisted largely of the suggestion that further consultation would be advisable. The board, to its credit, declined.
q: What does the writer imply about the report?

qGloss.zh: 关于这份报告，作者暗示了什么？

opts: It mainly served its author's interests
It was rejected for being too short
It persuaded the board to act at once

passage: My aunt maintained that she had never told a lie, a claim she supported by an elaborate system of things left unsaid. Asked whether she liked a gift, she would observe that it was "exactly the sort of thing one hopes to be given". It took me years to notice that she never specified by whom.
q: What does the writer suggest about the aunt?

qGloss.zh: 关于这位姑妈，作者暗示了什么？

opts: She often told small lies to be kind
She avoided lying through careful wording
She disliked receiving presents at all

passage: Translators are sometimes praised for being invisible, as though the highest achievement were to leave no fingerprints. Yet every choice (this word rather than that, a long sentence broken or left whole) is an act of interpretation. To pretend otherwise does the craft no service; it merely ensures that when the choices are good, the credit goes elsewhere.
q: What does "otherwise" in the last sentence refer to?

qGloss.zh: 最后一句里的 "otherwise" 指的是什么？

opts: That good choices earn proper credit
That long sentences must be broken up

passage: Oyelaran's history of the bicycle is plainly the work of a devoted enthusiast. No bolt goes undescribed; no dispute between rival inventors goes unrecorded. Readers who share the author's passion will find the book indispensable. Others may feel, somewhere around the fourth chapter on gear ratios, that devotion is not always enough.
q: What is the reviewer's attitude to the book?

qGloss.zh: 书评作者对这本书的态度是什么？

opts: Charmed by its style, troubled by its errors
Persuaded by its argument, doubtful of its sources
Impressed by its detail, unsure of its appeal
Bored by its subject, won over by its wit

passage: It would be rash to dismiss the findings outright, yet the enthusiasm with which they have been greeted owes more to what people wish were true than to the strength of the evidence. A single trial, conducted by researchers with an acknowledged stake in the outcome, is at best an invitation to further study. Whether it proves to be more than that remains to be seen.
q: Which best describes the writer's view of the findings?

qGloss.zh: 下面哪一项最符合作者对这些研究结果的看法？

opts: Too weak to deserve further study
Worth pursuing but far from proven

passage: The agent described the cottage as "full of character", a phrase I have since learned to translate. The character in question turned out to reside chiefly in the plumbing, which announced itself at night, and in a staircase that no two visitors have ever descended in the same manner. We bought it, of course. One does not argue with character.
q: What does the writer imply the phrase "full of character" really meant?

qGloss.zh: 作者暗示 "full of character" 这个说法实际上是什么意思？

opts: The house had a long and proud history
The previous owners were unusual people
The agent knew the house very well
The house had a number of faults

passage: Much is made of the claim that reading on paper aids memory, and there is something in it. But the studies usually cited compare a printed page with a screen that is also offering email, headlines and the weather. Remove those, and the gap narrows to almost nothing. What is being measured, one suspects, is not paper against glass but attention against its enemies.
q: What does the writer suggest the studies really show?

qGloss.zh: 作者认为这些研究真正说明了什么？

opts: Distraction, not the screen itself, weakens memory
Paper is clearly the better aid to memory
Memory cannot be reliably measured at all

passage: I write to thank the committee for so promptly confirming that my letter of last March had arrived, and to observe, with the greatest respect, that a confirmation is not quite the same thing as a reply. Should the committee find itself able to address the substance of my question before the summer, I would be most grateful. I remain, as ever, patient.
q: What is the writer's real purpose?

qGloss.zh: 作者写这封信的真正目的是什么？

opts: To say sorry for writing so often
To press for a proper answer
To thank the committee for its reply
